instruction:
There's a Next.js e-commerce app at `/app`. Users experience visual instability issues including layout shifts and generally a bad experience.

Your job is to assess the root cause of the user experience issues by using best practices in nexts and react and fix accordingly.

## Rules

- Don't break existing functionality
- Don't change existing class names, ids or data-testid on any of the components as tests rely on them

items.requirement: Prevent the color theme from visibly flickering on load by applying the saved theme (e.g. from localStorage) via an inline script in the document head that runs before React hydrates.
items.source_quote: Users experience visual instability issues including layout shifts and generally a bad experience.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading the page and inspecting inline <script> tags in the HTML head for code that reads a theme value from localStorage and applies it (via classList, className, setAttribute, data-theme, or style) before hydration.

items.requirement: Keep cumulative layout shift (CLS) under Google's 'good' threshold of 0.1 across page load, late-loading content, scrolling, and pagination interactions.
items.source_quote: visual instability issues including layout shifts
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading the page, waiting for late content, scrolling to the bottom and back to the top, clicking next/prev pagination, and confirming the browser's PerformanceObserver-measured session-window CLS score stays below 0.1.

items.requirement: Ensure the app still builds and runs successfully, responding with HTTP 200 at the root route.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by running the production build and start commands, then confirming a curl request to http://localhost:3000 returns HTTP status 200.

items.requirement: Ensure products still render on the page as product cards after the fixes are applied.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading the page and confirming at least one element with data-testid="product-card" appears in the DOM.

items.requirement: Optimize web font loading (e.g. font-display: swap) so a flash of invisible text (FOIT) does not occur while custom fonts load.
items.source_quote: using best practices in nexts and react and fix accordingly
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading the page and checking document.fonts for at least one FontFace whose display property equals "swap".

items.requirement: Give every rendered product image explicit width and height (or an equivalent non-auto aspect-ratio) so its box is reserved before the image loads, preventing layout shift.
items.source_quote: visual instability issues including layout shifts
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading the page, waiting for product cards to appear, and confirming every element with data-testid="product-image" has a width and height attribute, or a non-auto CSS aspect-ratio, reserving its space.

items.requirement: Leave all pre-existing class names, ids, and data-testid attributes on components unchanged while implementing the layout-stability fixes.
items.source_quote: Don't change existing class names, ids or data-testid on any of the components as tests rely on them
items.verification: A grader can verify this by diffing the class, id, and data-testid attributes on components between the original and fixed codebase (or rendered DOM) and confirming none of the pre-existing values were renamed or removed, which also underpins the data-testid selectors (e.g. product-card, product-image, next-page-btn, prev-page-btn) used throughout the verifier tests.
